To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an algorithm for solving a class stochastic optimization problems that is based on the idea of stochastic zeroth order gradient descent and showed that it is nearly optimal for a class of non-convex problems.

(i) the randomized stochastic gradient method is an asymptotically optimal method for solving a class nonconvex SP problems, (ii) it is also an asymptotically efficient method for solving convex SP problems, (iii) the randomized stochastic zeroth order method is asymptotically optimal for solving a class zeroth-order SP problems.
the randomized stochastic gradient method is able to compute approximate stationary points with nearly optimal rates of convergence in the nonconvex setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of SA type methods for solving a class nonlinear SP problems which are nonconvex and/or non-smooth, and the analysis of their convergence properties.
the development of stochastic optimization methods that are robust with respect to noise and that can be implemented with a limited amount of computational resources.
the development of new SA type methods for SP problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the stochastic first- and zeroth-order methods for non-convex stochastic programming are very promising.
stochastic optimization is the best method for solving stochastic optimization problems, while deterministic optimization is the best approach for solving deterministic optimization problems.
stochastic gradient methods, and in particular stochastic gradient descent, are the state-of-the-art method for solving large-scale optimization problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have introduced a new SA method for solving a general class of nonconvex SP problems.

we have developed a new class of SA methods, namely, RSG, which are capable to solve a broad range of nonlinear SP problems, including nonconvex problems, and have established the complexity of these algorithms for computing approximate stationary points.
we introduce new stochastic approximation ( SA ) type algorithms for solving a class nonlinear ( possibly nonconvex ) stochastic programming ( SP ) problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a stochastic gradient method for a non-convex problem with the same complexity as for a convex problem.

, for a large class of problems, stochastic optimization methods can be made to be as fast as deterministic optimization methods in the sense that they can find an $\epsilon$-optimal solution in $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{\epsilon})$ iterations.
the RSG method can be viewed as a natural extension of the Polyak-Ruppert averaging scheme to a randomized setting.
